A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Relign research work. All 15 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G, support comparison. Retained content can be matched despite reflow and table renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations in Table 2, scaling and hallucination analyses in Figures 5–8, and human validation on 150 cases in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds model-level Pass Rate comparisons and APIBench generalization results in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same indecisive actions, synthesized supervision, SFT-then-DPO procedure, and preference hierarchies. Expanded trajectory-collection details do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 adds out-of-domain evaluation on APIBench, covering HuggingFace, TorchHub, and Tensorhub API calls. This substantively extends evaluation beyond the ToolBench/StableToolBench/RelyToolBench family used in v2. Existing training coverage and original, missing-parameter, and unmatched-tools subsets remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same base models, closed-source comparators, RLHF, StepTool, SFT, DPO, and SFT&DPO comparisons. APIBench extends the existing LLaMA3.1-versus-Relign comparison under shared BM25 and oracle retrieval conditions; these are evaluation configurations rather than new competing alignment methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated DPO learning rate from 1e-6 to 1e-5. New APIBench evaluation uses BM25/oracle retrieval and AST accuracy without APIBench training. Section 2.2.1 also explicitly excludes failed tasks from RePR's hallucination deduction. The PDFs do not establish whether existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 extends the existing metric comparison by testing whether Relign's benefits persist under original Pass Rate across three model families. Section 4.5 adds an explicit distribution-shift test across APIBench domains and retrieval conditions. These substantively broaden validation; existing scaling analyses, hallucination breakdowns, human validation, and the appendix case study remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Appendix A retains the same human-validation reporting. Newly disclosed trajectory and preference-pair counts concern training-data construction, not statistical replication.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 add substantial results: LLaMA3.1's overall original Pass Rate is 82.6 versus 87.7 with Relign; APIBench HuggingFace/BM25 hallucination rates are 9.7 versus 6.4 and AST accuracy is 14.3 versus 15.7. These are newly reported comparisons, not version-to-version gains. Table 2 and existing plots remain unchanged. New Table 3 reports I3 RePR of 75.4 for LLaMA3.1+Relign, conflicting with 75.3 in retained Table 2. The model-size discussion also replaces the claimed decline in task hallucination with declining excessive tool calls.

T1.justification: Section 2.2.1 refines the definition underlying RePR by explicitly excluding tasks with zero original pass outcome from result-hallucination deductions, avoiding double punishment. The displayed formulas and alignment preference hierarchies otherwise remain unchanged; no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about hallucination categorization, reliability metrics, RelyToolBench, and Relign's reliability and efficiency benefits. Added evaluations support these claims without redefining the principal contributions.

C2.justification: The data-size discussion replaces speculation about noise and redundancy with an explanation centered on ToolBench's lack of failure cases. New passages interpret smaller PR–RePR gaps as reduced contamination of final answers and APIBench transfer as evidence of better tool-use strategies. These are additional interpretations, not newly demonstrated causal mechanisms.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly documents sampling temperature 0.7, multi-round collection from 10,000 tasks, 10,000–20,000 preference pairs, model-specific totals of 17,000/19,000/14,000, and training steps determined by collected pairs. It also states that no grid search was performed. The abstract changes a promised code/data release to reported availability with a repository address.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds five cited works covering API-documentation grounding, low-confidence hallucination detection, efficient tool calling, ToolBeHonest, and explicit knowledge-boundary modeling. These broaden contextual coverage while retaining the existing novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds two experimental subsections, renumbers Discussion to 4.6, expands training explanations, revises selected discussion and related-work paragraphs, and adds acknowledgments and updated affiliations. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 3–4, moves Figures 7–8 between columns, and reflows surrounding text and references. Appendix prompt tables are renumbered from 3–7 to 5–9. Existing figures retain their content, and the document keeps its established layout.

improvement.justification: The added standard Pass Rate comparison and APIBench test strengthen validation beyond v2's central evaluation, while clearer RePR handling, training disclosures, and reported code/data access improve transparency. Correcting the model-size discussion also improves agreement with Figure 8. These benefits outweigh limited reporting problems, including the new 75.4/75.3 discrepancy and the unexplained relationship between the revised DPO learning rate and unchanged main results.
